text: Self-improvement cycle 4: prevent zero-baseline intervention equality from producing a positive benchmark result
description: Observed limitation from the live paired benchmark: both graph-grounded and stateless conditions completed 4/4 tasks with zero interventions and zero policy violations, but the analyzer returned positive because `0 <= 0 * 0.8`. Frozen regression: equal zero interventions with equal completion and safety must be null. Bounded change: require graph-grounded mean interventions to be strictly lower as well as at most 80% of stateless before intervention reduction can establish positive. Re-run the existing complete test suite and re-analyze the exact preserved eight live records without rerunning agents.

reflections.context: The first live autonomy comparison exposed a zero-baseline relative-reduction defect in the frozen analyzer.
reflections.outcome: Added a regression asserting equal zero interventions is null, then required a strict absolute intervention decrease in addition to the 20% relative threshold. Re-analyzing the exact preserved eight records changed the result from mechanical positive to valid null. Verification: 106/106 tests, TypeScript, and git diff check pass.
reflections.effectiveness: The one-line predicate correction prevented a false capability claim without changing tasks, evidence, budgets, or rerunning agents. No safety or reliability regression was observed.
reflections.lesson: A percentage reduction is undefined as evidence of improvement at a zero baseline; require strict absolute improvement before applying a relative threshold.
reflections.pattern: Guard relative effect-size rules with directionality and zero-baseline tests.

status.comment: Bounded analyzer correction implemented, verified, and applied to preserved evidence; awaiting user acceptance.

valueRationale: Without this correction, equal zero-intervention outcomes can falsely establish a capability hypothesis.
